summary: An announcement for the first phase of the October 1971 Network Working Group meeting: a hands-on workshop at MIT's Project MAC for system programmers whose sites had working Telnet. Teams would test the network from MAC consoles to find remaining problems. Attendance was capped at about a dozen people.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo invites system programmers to a hands-on Telnet workshop at MIT Project MAC. Participants would test connections between hosts, find implementation problems and prepare reports for the Network Working Group meeting.

subtitle: An invitation to a small system-programmer workshop testing Telnet connections at Project MAC.

tldr.problem: Sites with operational Telnet needed to find remaining problems in protocol implementations before the Network Working Group meeting.
tldr.mechanism: A small group of system programmers would use Project MAC consoles to test possible Telnet connections and report results.

sections.title: The Workshop Invitation
sections.content:
The Network Working Group meeting was scheduled for MIT Project MAC in Cambridge, Massachusetts, October 10 to 14, 1971. Its first phase was a workshop for system programmers from sites with operational Telnet interfaces.

The organizers asked for no more than a dozen participants. They should understand protocols, their own NCPs and Telnet implementations. Sites were asked to register a participant with Anne Speare.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop was for a small group of system programmers whose sites had working Telnet. They were expected to understand their host software and network protocols.

sections.title: Testing Telnet Connections
sections.content:
The workshop begins at noon on Sunday, October 10, with a strategy meeting at Project MAC. The first task is to establish and test all possible Telnet connections with MAC's PDP-10, Host 70. Participants then pair up and use nested Telnet sessions to fill in a matrix of connections.

The organizers expect the teams to find implementation problems, discuss protocols and learn about a range of hosts. They plan to use the experience to inform later Network Working Group sessions.
sections.plainLanguage: The participants first test connections to the MAC host, then work through connections between host pairs. They record problems and report what they learn.

sections.title: Preparation and Follow-up
sections.content:
Project MAC is preparing documentation for its user Telnet and a booklet of scenarios for testing site use. It wants advice from participating hosts and plans to establish routine use before the workshop.

The organizers are working to stabilize their system and arrange hardware repair support. They hope knowledgeable people at other sites will be available to help solve minor problems during the tests. The workshop results will contribute to protocol review and status reports.
sections.plainLanguage: The organizers are preparing instructions, stable systems and repair support. Workshop findings will be used in reports and later discussions.
